trajectory_summary: The call starts with an unusually cooperative, highly informed customer who takes over pacing and content almost immediately; the rep never regains control, drifting into passive filler while the customer self-qualifies, self-pitches, and eventually coaches the rep on his own career. An appointment gets loosely set for 'Monday' but with no locked time and no button-up, leaving it structurally fragile despite the customer's apparent readiness.
outcome_dispute: V1 tag unknown but this should not be read as a clean booked win — no specific time was locked and button_up never occurred, so it is tentative/callback at best despite high customer receptivity.

observed_outcome.quote: Monday, you can call anytime. You know? Okay.
observed_outcome.reasoning: Customer agrees in principle to a specialist call on Monday but no specific time is locked, and button_up (time confirmation, 'is that fair' handshake, no-driving instruction) never occurs — the call ends abruptly after the customer's monologue.

bill_anchor_audit.reasoning: Bill amount ($250, 11,000 kWh) was captured at 02:36 but never referenced again to build urgency; the flip should have landed around 05:48 when the customer himself was calculating BGE cost projections — rep could have anchored back to the captured $250 as the current pain point being replaced.

bill_document_audit.ask_quote: I can send you a bill if you want.
bill_document_audit.result_quote: and I'll reply with I think it's March's bill, but you'll be able to see the past twelve months.
bill_document_audit.reasoning: Rep asked for the bill and the customer agreed to email it and said they'd reply with March's bill; it was not received on the call.

interest_reason_audit.reasoning: Customer stated he's 'looking to lease' at 01:22, but the rep never reinforced leasing as the reason for the appointment or tied the specialist meeting back to it explicitly.

primary_coaching_focus.topic: Failure to lock a specific appointment time
primary_coaching_focus.quote: Do you wanna just shoot for, like, tomorrow morning or afternoon?
primary_coaching_focus.why: Despite a highly engaged, self-qualifying customer, the call ends on 'Monday, you can call anytime' with no locked time and no button-up — this is the single biggest procedural miss given how easy this customer was to close.

key_moments.quote: So I guess question number one is do you guys just sell or do you lease?
key_moments.stewart_read: Customer hands the rep a direct qualifying/interest question up front and the rep answers vaguely instead of using it to anchor toward the specialist conversation.

key_moments.stewart_read: Customer states a cost-based reason for not buying (only leasing); rep does not flip this into bill-pain leverage, just continues the verify checklist.
